newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: CARACAS SHRS CLOSE OFF ON LACK OF FOREIGN INTEREST.
newsitem.headline: CARACAS SHRS CLOSE OFF ON LACK OF FOREIGN INTEREST.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed slightly lower in thin trade dominated by local investors, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share .IBC index fell 0.55 percent to 9,292.61, as 24 stocks fell, 13 rose and seven closed flat.
Brokers said foreign investors continued to shun the market due to upcoming U.S. Federal Reserve talks and uncertainty over Venezuela's labor situation.
"The market continues to be sluggish due to the absence of foreign investors," said Cavelba broker Harold Cuellar.
Brokers forecast prices would drift lower in coming sessions before resuming an upward trend toward the end of the week.

"There's no fundamental reason for the market to fall. What is being felt is that the big foreign investors, which raise volume and push up prices, are staying out," another broker said. Volume was slim with 1,173 trades for 3.400 billion bolivars ($6.9 million), the exchange said.
Among leading stocks, Electricidad de Caracas fell 1.00 bolivar to 812.00 bolivars and telephone company CANTV rose 5.50 bolivars to 3,060.50 bolivars.
